hypothesis: Geodesics and Jacobi fields are intrinsic: an ambient rotation changes only the embedded coordinates (which rotate exactly), and the choice of reference basis for headings is a relabeling; an orientation-reversing basis changes the meaning of '+eps' and of the normal together, so a consistently expressed first-order (Jacobi) separation is unchanged; the finite-eps separation is unchanged exactly only where it is odd in eps.
input_data: Sphere, Torus(2, 1), Saddle(1), GaussianBump(0.5, 1) on declared paths; HyperbolicPlane(1) for basis changes
Rotations: axis (1, 2, 3) angle 0.7; axis (0, 0, 1) angle 1.0472; axis (1, -1, 0) angle 2.5

Basis angles beta = 0.3, 1.1, 2.5, -2; RK4 with N = 64; orientation test on the unit sphere with eps = 0.001, L = 2, and on Torus(2, 1) from (0, 0.3), heading 0.5, L = 3 with eps = 0.001, 0.01, 0.04 (RK4 N = 64, checked at 128)
mathematical_model: Rotated(base, R): X' = R X, so X'_i . X'_j = X_i . X_j and the second fundamental form is unchanged; in exact arithmetic the chart ODE is identical. A basis (e1', e2') rotated by beta with heading h - beta yields the same unit tangent. In the left-handed basis (e1, -e2) the heading -h + eps is the right-handed heading h - eps, and its +90 degree normal is -N. With d(eps) = J_eps . N = eps j + C2 eps^2 + ..., the left-handed run measured along -N is -d(-eps) = eps j - C2 eps^2 + ..., so (J_eps . (-N)) equals the right-handed J_eps . N to first order in eps; the eps^2 parts have opposite signs, so the finite separations agree exactly only where the separation is odd in eps, as on the unit sphere (sin(s) sin(eps)), and otherwise own/right - 1 = -2 C2 eps / j + O(eps^2).
numerical_result: Rotation: max state difference 1.8e-15, endpoint rotation error 1.4e-15, curvature difference 2e-15; basis rotation: max state difference 1.8e-15; unit sphere: left-handed '+eps' along N: ratio -1.000000000002; along its own normal: ratio 1.000000000002; right-handed separation minus sin(L) sin(eps) 8.4e-12; torus: own/right - 1 = -0.0004763, -0.004753, -0.01885 for eps = 0.001, 0.01, 0.04 (log-log slope 0.9972); reflection refused: 'Frame change requires a proper rotation matrix'.
observation_model: Chart states (u, v, Jacobi columns) at every node, embedded endpoints, curvature along the path, and the signed embedded separation along the base geodesic's in-surface normal (N, or -N for the left-handed basis).

title: Test frame-change invariance under rotations and tangent-basis changes.
uncertainty: Roundoff differences depend on platform arithmetic (observed up to 1.8e-15); the regression tolerances allow 1e-11. On the unit sphere the orientation ratios differ from -1 and +1 by at most 2.5e-12: RK4 truncation of the +eps and -eps runs, not a second-order eps term, because the exact sphere separation is odd in eps. On the torus the gap own/right - 1 is a second-order term of the separation, not truncation: it changes by 9.9e-08 relative from N = 64 to 128, and its slope in eps is within 0.0035 of the consecutive-eps slopes.
unresolved_assumptions: Rotations only; translations and reflections of the embedding are not exercised
Hyperbolic-plane isometries (Mobius maps) are not tested, only basis changes
The orientation test uses one sphere path and one torus path; saddle and bump are covered only by the basis-rotation test, and the coefficient C2 of the torus gap is measured, not derived
